title: Water pump weep hole leak (colored drip under the engine)

beats.shot: Macro close-up: colored fluid drips from under a parked engine bay onto clean concrete
beats.prompt: macro close up shot of colored coolant fluid dripping slowly from the underside of a car engine bay onto a clean concrete garage floor, shallow depth of field, cinematic lighting, photorealistic
beats.vo: A few drops of colored fluid under the front of your engine isn't always the radiator.

beats.shot: Engine bay wide shot pushing toward the front-center pulley and serpentine belt driving the water pump
beats.prompt: wide shot of a car engine bay pushing in toward the front center pulley and serpentine belt assembly driving a water pump, bright shop lighting, photorealistic, cinematic camera movement
beats.vo: Water pumps have a tiny weep hole built in — it's designed to leak a little before it fails.

beats.shot: Extreme macro of the weep hole on the water pump housing with a faint drip trail
beats.prompt: extreme macro close up of a small drain weep hole on a car water pump housing, a faint colored drip trail visible below it, engine bay detail, photorealistic
beats.vo: That hole lets coolant escape early, instead of the seal blowing out with no warning.

beats.shot: Close-up of the translucent coolant overflow reservoir with a light residue stain near the cap
beats.prompt: close up of a translucent car coolant overflow reservoir tank showing colored fluid level inside, a faint dried residue stain around the cap on the outside, engine bay lighting, photorealistic
beats.vo: One clue: it's colored and sticky — not clear water like AC condensation.

beats.shot: Macro of dried, crusty residue near a pump housing bolt, no active drip
beats.prompt: macro close up of dried crusty mineral residue buildup trailing down from a car water pump housing bolt, no active dripping, engine bay detail, photorealistic
beats.vo: You might also see a dried, crusty residue trail near the pump before a puddle ever shows up.

beats.shot: Dash close-up: temperature gauge needle drifting toward hot
beats.prompt: close up of a car dashboard temperature gauge needle slowly drifting from the normal center position toward the hot zone, dim interior lighting, photorealistic
beats.vo: Ignore it long enough and the engine can overheat with no warning.

beats.shot: Wide static hold: clean automotive service bay, no signage/logo
beats.prompt: wide static shot of a clean automotive service bay interior, bright even lighting, no visible signage, logos, or text, photorealistic, held static frame
beats.vo: Stop by and we'll take a look.

igfbCopy.primaryCaption: A few drops of colored fluid under the front of your engine isn't always "just the radiator." Water pumps are built with a tiny weep hole that leaks a little before the seal fails for good. Catch it early and it's a simple fix — ignore it and it can mean overheating on the road. Stop by and we'll take a look.

adVariants.hook: That small puddle under your car might be a built-in warning.
adVariants.caption: Water pumps have a weep hole on purpose — it drips a little before the seal fails completely. Catching it now beats a tow later.
adVariants.cta: Stop by and we'll take a look — no guessing.

adVariants.hook: Colored drops under the engine, not under the AC?
adVariants.caption: That's coolant, not condensation — and it's often the first sign a water pump seal is wearing out. One clue: it's sticky, not clear.
adVariants.cta: Worth a quick look — swing by.
